notable_issues: submit() awaits the coroutine inside the semaphore, so the semaphore slot is held for the entire duration — this means concurrency is correctly bounded, but the task is not truly 'submitted' to run independently; it blocks the caller AND holds the slot, making the _tasks tracking and shutdown gather partially redundant

Double-check of self._shutdown after acquiring the semaphore creates a race window: between the first check and semaphore acquisition, shutdown() sets the flag AND gathers tasks — but since the task isn't added to _tasks yet, shutdown can complete before this submit finishes, violating shutdown semantics

map() launches all submit() calls via gather simultaneously — each submit acquires the semaphore, so all coroutines are created eagerly as tasks via ensure_future even before the semaphore is acquired, potentially spawning more concurrent coroutines than intended
